description: Weekly domain-grouped updates, two ordinary PRs per repository, separate majors, and review before every merge.
prHeader: Review required: check dependency impact and CI before merging. Routine domain groups and separate major upgrades share two PR slots per repository; queued updates wait for a slot and the next Monday run, and the repository's Dependency Dashboard issue lists them.

packageRules.description: Group routine minor, patch, digest, and pin updates; later rules split operational domains.
Refresh npm ranges even when the newest eligible version already satisfies the old range.
Group routine development dependencies separately from application runtime dependencies.

Group routine container image tag, digest, and initial pin updates from Dockerfiles, Compose files, and other image references no later rule claims. Images referenced from Kubernetes, Helm, Flux, Kustomize, Argo CD, or Terraform files go to infrastructure, and images in GitHub workflows, devcontainers, or pre-commit go to ci and development environment, because those later rules take precedence.

Group routine updates from managers in Renovate's kubernetes and terraform categories (Kubernetes, Helm, Helmfile, Flux, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Terraform, Terragrunt), including the container images those files reference.

Group routine updates from the github-actions, devcontainer, and pre-commit managers, including action digests, images those files reference, and the Renovate runner version. Other CI systems and tool-version files such as mise or asdf are not matched and stay in earlier groups.
Keep major upgrades separate from routine groups and preserve Renovate's related-package groups; never automerge.
Preserve first-party codeOps workflow and action branch refs without digest pinning; retain other update handling

Owner rule (1 of 2): report Python patch updates apart from minor ones so rule 2 can hold minors without hiding patches. No matchUpdateTypes here because Renovate reads separateMinorPatch before an update type exists.

Owner rule (2 of 2): never propose Python minor or major bumps such as 3.14 to 3.15; patch (3.14.7 to 3.14.8), digest and pin updates still flow. Matches by package name in every manager: python and other registry python images, setup-python python-version inputs, .python-version, requires-python, runtime.txt, and mise, asdf, proto, devbox, pixi, poetry and devcontainer pins. The setup-python action and the devcontainer python feature are not Python releases and are not matched. To move Python on purpose, edit the pin by hand or add a narrow enabled: true packageRule in the consumer repository.

Owner rule (2026-10-21): every major, minor and patch update (including npm range bumps and lock-file-only updates, which are flags on those) and every digest update waits 4 days after publication before Renovate raises it, in every consumer. A release without a publication timestamp stays pending (timestamp-required, Renovate's default since v42, stated so any consumer override is explicit). Renovate's docker datasource reads dates only from Docker Hub, so images on ghcr.io, quay.io, registry.k8s.io, mcr.microsoft.com and other registries stay pending until the consumer maps them to a digest-identical Docker Hub repository with overridePackageName. Digest updates of floating tags (latest, lts-alpine) are never dated by Renovate 44 and stay pending: pin a versioned tag instead. git-refs, git-tags and undated custom datasources stay pending too. Pin, pinDigest, replacement, lockFileMaintenance and rollback updates carry no release date and are not held. Vulnerability-fix PRs still bypass this through vulnerabilityAlerts. See docs/decisions/0001-fleet-release-age-soak.md.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), part 2: first-party images on GHCR are built by this fleet's own CI, not by an upstream that could be compromised, so they are not held by the release-age soak. GHCR publishes no release dates, so without this every ghcr.io/moosegooseconsulting and ghcr.io/coldaine image would be held forever. Matching is case-insensitive.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), part 3: first-party GitHub actions, workflows and releases are this fleet's own code, so they are not held. Scoped to GitHub datasources so the same names on another registry (for example an unclaimed Docker Hub namespace) stay soaked.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), part 4: GitHub-hosted runner labels and the language-runtime version lists (python-version, java-version, dart-version) publish no release dates in Renovate 44, so the soak would hold them forever, including Python patch releases the 2026-10-13 Python rule keeps flowing for security. They name official toolchain releases rather than packages a third party can publish, so they are not held. Runtimes with dated datasources (node-version, golang-version, ruby-version, dotnet-version) stay soaked.

vulnerabilityAlerts.prHeader: Review required: check dependency impact and CI before merging. This is a security fix: it is not scheduled, not held for release age, and does not use or wait for the repository's two ordinary PR slots.
